chunks: From him, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamzah, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'When the young boy is visited by death and has not reached puberty, his will is valid for his close relatives (kin) and is not valid for strangers.'

key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: The young boy/child, specifically in the context of pre-puberty
key_terms.ذَوِي الْأَرْحَامِ: Close relatives / kin (those entitled to inheritance but not necessarily fixed-share heirs)

ai.seo_question: Is a child's will valid for relatives if they die before puberty?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that a pre-pubescent boy (ghulam) possesses limited testamentary capacity, valid only for his extended kin (dhawi al-arham) rather than strangers, reflecting the principle that his estate is primarily his own but subject to familial rights. This ruling distinguishes his status from that of a fully mature adult, ensuring that his modest assets are distributed according to familial ties rather than general bequests. The narration, found in Al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam, underscores the practical application of inheritance laws to minors who have not yet reached the age of legal discretion.
